headline: Probabilistic and self-supervised models extract spatial cell states and niche programs
label: Spatial Omics Latent Models
summary: New spatial omics preprints add 3D cell shape, niche programs and spatial multi-omic priors; histology-to-omics inference itself is absent from this set.
synthesis: The current items do not center on histology-to-omics prediction; they share a focus on structured latent models for spatial and single-cell omics. multiCAsp applies a graph-Laplacian spatial prior to joint multi-omic factor analysis. CIRCA targets identifiable cell and niche programs and their links to tissue pathology through self-supervised causal representation learning. A rotation-equivariant network reconstructs 3D cell shape from transcript point clouds, and the resulting embeddings improve protein prediction. CASTLE adds cell-type-aware spatial graphs and contrastive learning to domain detection. MiSA extends spatial statistics to HiPR-FISH microbiome images, testing disease-associated dysbiosis. TMCells, Echidna and the hybrid mixture model are adjacent probabilistic methods for non-spatial single-cell and biomedical data. The new element is the emphasis on interpretable, identifiable spatial representations.
